entities.name: Artsakh State Museum
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Artsakh State Museum (Armenian: Արցախի Պետական Թանգարան) in Stepanakert (Khankendi), the capital of the Republic of Artsakh (Nagorno-Karabakh) — a de facto independent Armenian-majority republic in the South Caucasus whose status has been one of the most intractable post-Soviet territorial conflicts — housed collections documenting Armenian cultural heritage in the Karabakh region, including archaeological materials from ancient Artsakh (one of the traditional provinces of ancient Armenia), medieval Armenian Christian churches, and modern Armenian cultural materials.

The Nagorno-Karabakh conflict (1988-1994, 2020, 2023) between Armenia and Azerbaijan over the Armenian-majority enclave within Soviet Azerbaijan's administrative borders is one of the most complex and tragic territorial disputes of the post-Soviet era. The Artsakh State Museum's existence and collections were central to Armenian claims of centuries-old cultural heritage in the region — a heritage Azerbaijanis disputed and re-interpreted as Azerbaijani Caucasian Albanian heritage.

In September 2023, Azerbaijan's military offensive (Operation Vengeance) recaptured the entirety of Nagorno-Karabakh, causing the mass exodus of over 100,000 Armenians from the region within days. The Republic of Artsakh dissolved on January 1, 2024. The fate of the Artsakh State Museum's collections — and of Armenian cultural heritage in Nagorno-Karabakh generally — became an urgent international concern, with fears that Armenian churches, monasteries, and museum collections would be destroyed or re-attributed under Azerbaijani control.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Artsakh State Museum — preserving Armenian cultural heritage in one of the world's most intractable post-Soviet territorial disputes, dissolved with the Republic of Artsakh in January 2024 — is historically significant as a monument to the cultural dimension of the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict and the fate of cultural heritage in contested territories.
